items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: there’s a piece on the last album that Future Man and I wrote together called “New Math”

ctx.x: I really enjoyed a couple of things on “Live Art” that stuck out. When you nailed — there’s a vocal tune on there, “O Darlin’” and when you nailed that six-eight groove, and then, later on in the CD you start playing a folk song from North Korea. To me that’s like, well this man has heard and absorbed an awful lot of music.

Well I love music but to me it’s more all similar than it is different. It’s not that — I mean a great folk tune from the United States and a great folk tune from North Korea aren’t that different. And when you hear this version of it you can hear that pretty clearly. Like that Korean tune is a simple pentatonic tune and we have tons of them here so it’s just a different tune. You’re just learning the tune. It’s not — I mean there are things that we’ve done that I think are like an achievement and for me like on…
And it’s a nice sort of release when it comes in the record I think. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
